title: How would you describe this sound?
description: A listening study about the character of short synthesizer sounds.

descriptors.label: Brightness
descriptors.definition: How much high-frequency or treble character does this sound have?

descriptors.label: Roughness
descriptors.definition: How much rapid fluttering, beating or grating texture does this sound have?

descriptors.label: Percussiveness
descriptors.definition: How much does this sound resemble a struck or plucked event, with a distinct onset followed by a fall in sound level?

descriptors.label: Sustainedness
descriptors.definition: How strongly does this sound have a continuing, held quality after it begins?

scale.unclear_label: I cannot judge / the term is unclear

experience_question.label: Which of these have you done yourself?
experience_question.help: Select one or more examples you have actually done. Personal practice counts; it does not need to be released or professional work. Extra details are optional.
experience_question.placeholder: For example: I practised a song on piano and varied the touch to shape its tone.

experience_tools_label: Which instruments, vocal activities or music tools have you used?
experience_tools_placeholder: For example: piano, bass guitar, singing, a DAW or a synthesizer
resume_instructions: You may close this tab and return to the same study link using the same browser profile on the same device while the study is open. Avoid private/incognito mode and do not clear this site's data. Your invitation starts one session; it cannot restore a session in a different browser. Each saved response is kept; an unfinished answer may need to be entered again.
information: This study investigates how people describe the sound character (timbre) of synthesizer sounds. Your judgments will help develop and evaluate models of perceived sound qualities.

You will listen to 20 different synthesizer sounds and rate four aspects of their character: brightness, roughness, percussiveness and sustainedness. There are 3 practice sounds first and a break after study sound 10. Allow approximately 10–15 minutes, depending on replays and breaks.

Play each sound fully at least once. For each quality, choose a rating from 1 (not at all) to 7 (very). Select I cannot judge / the term is unclear when you cannot make that judgment. There is no correct answer supplied by the researcher.

You can correct the immediately previous response before starting the next sound. Your original answers and any corrections are retained. Use Save and continue to save each response. You cannot skip unanswered sounds.

Participation is voluntary. Pause or stop at any time. Use headphones in a quiet place, set a comfortable volume and stop if listening becomes uncomfortable. Your experience answers, ratings, playback counts, times and feedback are saved under a participant code. Please do not enter names, email addresses or identifying links. Hosting providers may keep technical access logs.

You may withdraw using this browser while you retain session access, or contact the researcher with your listener code. Withdrawal excludes responses from analysis; saved audit records are not immediately erased.

eligibility.rule: Adult volunteer with practical experience in music production, sound design, synth patch creation, instrumental performance or singing, supported by a self-reported practical example. Personal practice counts; passive music listening alone does not qualify.

retention_statement: Responses are stored for research analysis and project assessment with access restricted to the research team. No automatic deletion date has been set. Contact the researcher with your listener code to ask about stored responses or request withdrawal.
withdrawal_statement: You may withdraw using this browser while you retain session access, or contact the researcher with your listener code. Withdrawn responses are excluded from analysis. Withdrawal does not immediately erase saved audit records.
participant_notice: C1 listening study. Completed study responses are collected for research analysis; practice responses are excluded.
